title: speicher.md instance config
description: Admin-controlled. Never lives in a content repo. Only this file may use ${VAR} interpolation.

mail.description: Configure SMTP to send sign-in links. Required for magic-link providers.

host.description: Enter your SMTP hostname, such as `smtp.example.com`.

port.description: Enter your SMTP port. Port `465` uses TLS immediately; other ports use STARTTLS if available.

username.description: Enter your SMTP username. Omit if your server needs no authentication.

password.description: Enter your SMTP password or an environment variable reference, such as `${SMTP_PASSWORD}`.

from.description: Enter an allowed sender address, optionally as `Name <address>`. Defaults to the brand name and the `username` email address, or `noreply@<public-host>` from `SPEICHER_PUBLIC_URL`.

reply_to.description: Enter a reply address if replies should go somewhere other than the sender.

assets.description: Where asset bytes live. Metadata and ACLs always stay in Postgres; the browser never talks to the store directly — every read is proxied through the app after the authz check.

path.description: filesystem: volume mount path. Single replica, or an RWX volume.

endpoint.description: s3: for non-AWS providers such as Hetzner Object Storage or MinIO. azure: a blob endpoint other than `https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net` — a sovereign cloud, or Azurite in development. Give the account URL, not the container's: the container is appended.

container.description: azure: the container, which this instance never creates — a data-plane role cannot, so it is the operator's to make.

auth.description: azure: how this instance proves who it is, and the default is `key` because it is the one an operator configuring this from a browser already has. `key` and `connection_string` are secrets this instance holds; a managed identity avoids holding one and is worth moving to once the storage account and this deployment are in the same directory. `managed_identity` is the identity of the host — a VM, Container App or App Service — and `workload_identity` is the federated token an AKS pod is handed; they are different mechanisms and the wrong one fails as a timeout rather than as a refusal, so it is named here rather than guessed. `default` walks the SDK's whole chain including the developer's `az` login: it is a development convenience, and in production it means no single answer to which identity this is running as — so `/-/config` does not offer it there.

connection_string.description: azure: required when `auth` is `connection_string`. It carries its own endpoint, so `endpoint` is not consulted alongside it.

account_key.description: azure: the storage account key, required when `auth` is `key`. A long-lived shared secret that grants the whole account — prefer a managed identity, which grants a role on one container and cannot be copied out of the process.

client_id.description: azure: the user-assigned identity to use, when `auth` resolves a token. Absent means the system-assigned one. Under `workload_identity` the AKS webhook normally injects this into the pod as `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` and the SDK reads it — set it here only to override that.

tenant_id.description: azure: the directory to authenticate against, when `auth` is `workload_identity` and the environment does not already say.

presign_over_bytes.description: Assets larger than this are delivered by presigned redirect after the authz check, instead of proxied. 0 disables presigning. Never applied to inline images.

presign_ttl.description: Presigned URLs are bearer capabilities valid until expiry regardless of the ACL. Keep short.

theme.description: How pages look: the template, the typeface and colour overrides. Changes apply right away and never trigger a sync.

template.description: The template for all pages: `default`, `blueprint`, `editorial` or `workspace`. An unknown name falls back to `default`.

font.description: The typeface of the body text. Each value uses fonts already installed on the reader's device; web fonts are not loaded.

rounded_corners.description: Whether corners are rounded. Off sets every corner radius to 0, whatever the template chooses.

tui.description: Whether pages look like a terminal: monospace text, square corners and terminal-style headings, links and lists. Works with every template.

palette.description: The palette replaces individual colours of the template. It is used to match the documentation and the admin pages to your brand colours. Colours you leave empty keep the default colours.

light.description: Colours for readers in light mode.

dark.description: Colours for readers in dark mode. Left out, the template's dark colours are used.

brand.description: The name, logos and favicon in the page header and browser tab. Only the instance sets these; repositories cannot.

name.description: The name shown at the top of every page, linking to the home page. It is also the logo's alt text. Without it, the header shows the host of `SPEICHER_PUBLIC_URL`.

show_name.description: Whether the name is shown beside the logo. Turn it off if your logo already contains the name. Without a logo, the name is always shown.

name_align.description: How the name lines up with the logo: `center` centres it on the logo's height, `bottom` sets it on the logo's bottom edge.

logo.description: The header logo: a PNG, WebP or SVG of at most 1 MB, as a `data:` URI or a `sha256:` reference to an uploaded image. Used in dark mode too, unless `logo_dark` is set.

logo_dark.description: The header logo for readers in dark mode: a PNG, WebP or SVG of at most 1 MB, as a `data:` URI or a `sha256:` reference to an uploaded image.

icon.description: The favicon shown in the browser tab: a square PNG or SVG of at most 1 MB, as a `data:` URI or a `sha256:` reference to an uploaded image. A PNG must be at least 32×32 pixels.

wallpaper.description: Wallpaper behind the pages as base64 data URI (max 5 MB JPEG, PNG, WebP or SVG)

wallpaper_dark.description: Wallpaper for dark mode as base64 data URI (max 5 MB JPEG, PNG, WebP or SVG)

wallpaper_all_themes.description: Whether the uploaded wallpaper is shown in every theme. When this is turned off, only themes with a wallpaper of their own, such as Glass, show it.

attribution.description: Whether pages show `Published with speicher.md` at the bottom, linking to the speicher.md website. The text cannot be changed.

graph.description: Features built from the links between pages: the related column, hover previews, tags and link-weighted search. speicher.md records links on every sync, so changes apply right away. A reader only sees links between pages they can read.

enabled.description: Turns all link graph features on or off. When off, the settings below have no effect.

related.description: Shows a column beside each article with the pages it links to and the pages that link to it.

previews.description: Shows the title and description of the target page when a reader hovers over a link to another page. Links to pages the reader cannot open get no preview.

terms.description: Shows a page's frontmatter `tags` as chips, each leading to a list of the pages with that tag that the reader can open.

search_boost.description: Ranks a search result higher when other results of the same search link to it. It changes only the order of results.

related_limit.description: The most entries shown in each list of the related column.

analytics.description: Counts page reads and searches without results. Off by default. Stores no identities: unique readers are an estimate that cannot be traced back to a person.

enabled.description: Turns read analytics on. Turning it off stops counting and deletes all stored counts at the next maintenance run.

timezone.description: The time zone days are counted in, as an IANA name such as `Europe/Berlin`.

granularity.description: Whether reads are counted per `day` or per `hour`. Hourly counts show when people read, which can require agreement with a works council. Switching back to `day` deletes the hourly counts.

unique_readers.description: Estimate how many different signed-in people read each page per day. Anonymous readers and reads counted by the browser script are not included.

public_beacon.description: Count reads of public pages with a small script in the browser, because cached pages never reach the server. The script sends only the page path, with no cookie or identifier.

retention_days.description: How many days read counts are kept.

search_retention_days.description: How many days searches without results are kept.

notify.description: Emails about failed syncs, repositories that stopped syncing and expiring grants. Requires `mail`.

sync_failure.description: Who is emailed when a repository's sync fails, and again when it recovers. `committer` is the commit author, mailed only if they are a maintainer by email or have signed in with that address; otherwise the maintainers are mailed.

stale_after.description: How long a repository may go without syncing before it is reported, for example `12h`. A repository with a poll interval is given at least twice that interval.

expiry_warning.description: How long before an individual grant ends speicher.md starts warning about it, for example `7d`.

embedding.description: Connects an embedding model for semantic search. Any endpoint that offers the OpenAI embeddings API works, such as OpenAI, Azure OpenAI or Ollama. speicher.md only creates embeddings and never generates text. Changes apply after a restart.

base_url.description: The endpoint's address without `/embeddings`, for example `https://api.openai.com/v1`. speicher.md appends `/embeddings`.

api_key.description: The API key, sent as a bearer token and as an `api-key` header. Leave it out for an endpoint without authentication.

model.description: The name of the embedding model, as the endpoint expects it.

dimensions.description: The length of the vectors the model returns. Web and worker check it at startup and do not start if the model returns a different length.

send_dimensions.description: Whether to send `dimensions` with each request. Models that can shorten their vectors accept it; turn it off for models that reject it.

batch_size.description: How many passages are sent in one request.

max_concurrency.description: How many requests are sent at the same time. Lower it if a hosted endpoint rejects requests for exceeding its rate limit.

auth.description: Optional, and absent on an instance nobody has configured yet: there is then no way to sign in, so every caller holds `group:public` and nothing else. Present means at least one provider — absent and present-but-empty are different claims, and only the first is a fresh instance.

default_provider.description: Provider assumed when an individual grant omits `provider`. Without it, an unqualified grant is rejected — never guessed.

admins.description: Who administers this instance: the people and groups who can open the configuration and sync status of every repository under `/-/`. Administrators get no read access to content from this. A configuration that leaves nobody as administrator cannot be saved.

groups.description: Groups whose members are administrators. Each must be a group defined under `groups`, and at least one administrator group needs members unless `users` names someone.

users.description: Individual administrators, each named by `email`, or by `subject` with a `note`.

groups.description: References another speicher.md group by its internal name. All members of the referenced groups will be members of this group.

public.description: Repositories that may publish pages to visitors who are not signed in. Listing a repository only allows it: its own `access` must also name `public`.

repos.description: Repositories as `<owner>/<repository>`, the owner being the account or organization the repository belongs to, even where its URL leaves the owner out. Each listed repository may grant `access` to `public`.

forges.description: Where documentation is read from. Optional, and may be empty: an instance with no content source loads, serves nothing and can be administered — which is the state every instance is in before its first source is configured, and the state it returns to when the last one is removed. Requiring one meant the first boot needed a forge the operator could not add until the instance was running.

defaults.description: Starting values for every repository. A repository's root `.speicher.yaml` changes them the same way a folder's file does.

cover.description: A default cover image, as a path relative to each repository's root. Every repository needs that file.

colour.description: A colour, as a hex triplet. Three digits or six, because both are what a brand guide prints and expanding one is arithmetic. Nothing else: a token value is a place the CSS parser will also accept `url(https://…)`, and a stylesheet that can name a selector can report which pages a reader can open.

palette.description: Every colour the base sheet chooses, and no other: the six that carry a page, the two highlight pairs, the five callout accents and the fourteen the syntax highlighter maps onto. A colour a template derives from one of these — punctuation in code, the four status colours, a repository cover — is not here, because deriving it is the answer: move the neutral and quiet text, hairlines and operators in code move with it. `bg`, `fg` and `accent` are the three worth setting; leave `muted`, `line` and `surface` empty and they are mixed from the background and text colours in force, which is how a two-colour answer stays coherent instead of leaving hairlines and quiet text at the template's contrast against somebody else's background. Everything else left empty keeps the template's own.

accent.description: Links, focus rings and anything the eye is meant to go to.

muted.description: Quiet text — captions, metadata, punctuation in code. Mixed from `fg` and `bg` when unset.

line.description: Rules, borders and table hairlines. Mixed from `fg` and `bg` when unset.

surface.description: Panels that sit on the page — code blocks, the tree, table heads. Mixed from `fg` and `bg` when unset.

warn-bg.description: Behind a warning strip — the banner over a page whose repository is failing to sync.

warn-fg.description: The words on that strip. It is read against `warn-bg` and against nothing else.

mark-bg.description: Behind a search term highlighted in a result snippet.

callout-info.description: The `info` callout, and the note icon beside it.

callout-warning.description: The `warning` callout. It also colours the `warn` state on the operational surface.

callout-danger.description: The `danger` callout, and the `fail` state on the operational surface.

code-attr.description: Markup attribute names, and object keys.

code-variable.description: Variables, and interpolations inside a string.

code-inserted.description: An added line in a diff.

code-deleted.description: A removed line in a diff.

repoId.description: What a repository may be called here: the character set a forge allows, up to a hundred characters — an operator naming a repository copies what the forge calls it, and `Design.System` or `docs_v2` are ordinary names. Not `shortId`, which is what a forge id and a provider id are: those appear in URLs, and this does not. The URL segment is `slug`, which defaults to this and is slugged, so an id with a capital or a dot still serves a lowercase path. The first character must be alphanumeric, which is the whole of what this restriction is for: the id names a directory under the mirror root, and `.`, `..`, a hidden name and a leading `-` — which git and ssh read as an option — are what a name joined into a path must not be. A repository actually called `.github` therefore takes an id that is not its name, which the id was always allowed to be.

type.description: Selects the OpenID Connect provider. Use it for any provider that supports OpenID Connect, such as Google, Keycloak or Okta.

display_name.description: The name the sign-in page shows for this provider, for example `Google`. Defaults to the provider's id.

issuer.description: The address of the provider's OpenID Connect server, for example `https://accounts.google.com`. speicher.md reads the provider's settings from `<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`, and refuses an issuer that does not name a single tenant or realm.

client_id.description: The client id of the application you registered for speicher.md at the provider.

client_secret.description: The client secret of that application. Leave it out only if the provider registered speicher.md as a public client.

subject_claim.description: The claim in the sign-in token that holds the person's permanent id. Most providers use `sub`.

groups_claim.description: The claim in the sign-in token that lists the person's groups. Without it, or if the provider sends none (such as Google), the person belongs to no provider groups and can only be added to groups by email or subject.

email_claim.description: The claim in the sign-in token that holds the person's email address. Access granted by email is matched against it.

domains.description: Offer this provider only for addresses at these domains. Absent means it is offered for every address.

session_ttl.description: How long a sign-in stays valid. Groups are read only at sign-in, so a removed group membership keeps working until the session ends.

connection_idle_ttl.description: If you have a directory configured, this is how long a connection persists while not used. Without a directory, a connection ends with `session_ttl`.

directory.description: Optional read access to the provider's directory. speicher.md uses it to resolve email grants to people, count group members and notice people who have left.

type.description: Selects the magic-link provider, which signs people in with a link sent to their email address. Needs `mail`.

display_name.description: The name the sign-in page shows for this provider, for example `Email link`. Defaults to the provider's id.

token_ttl.description: How long a sign-in link stays valid after it is sent. A link can be used only once.

session_ttl.description: How long a sign-in stays valid.

same_browser.description: Whether a link only works in the browser it was requested from. Turn it off to let people request a link on one device and open it on another.

domains.description: Offer this provider only for addresses at these domains. Absent means it is offered for every address.

groupSource.description: The source of a group membership. Can be a directory group id, an email domain for a magic-link provider, one persons email, or a reference to another group by its internal name. Exactly one of the five keys must be present.

provider.description: Short ID of the identity provider you want to reference.

id.description: Group id as the provider emits it in groups_claim (oidc), or "org/team-slug" (github).

subject.description: Value of the provider's subject_claim, naming one person rather than a mapping. For a magic-link provider the subject IS the lowercased email address. The strongest of the four keys: a subject is assigned by the provider and cannot be set by the person it identifies, so it survives a rename and cannot be claimed by somebody else.

email.description: Address of one person, matched against the provider's email_claim. Mutable, reassignable, and on some providers set by a directory administrator rather than proven by the mailbox — so this is the convenient form and `subject` is the durable one. Refused on a provider whose issuer does not name one directory; see the loader.

group.description: The internal name of another group. Every member of that group is a member of this one.

note.description: Optional free text for later reference.

until.description: Optional expiry date. A group source will loose effect after this date. If it's not set the source will be permanent.

domain.description: Email domain as the group. magic-link providers only. The "address already appears in some ACL" check that gates link sending includes domain membership. Never use a freemail domain — it would grant anyone who can receive mail there.

type.description: The kind of source. `github` reads repositories through a GitHub App; `git` reads repositories you list from any git server over HTTPS or SSH.

primary.description: Whether this source's id is left out of its repositories' URLs. Only one source can be primary; when there is only one source, it is primary. Repositories of other sources are served under `/<source-id>/…`.

default_repository_owner.description: The user or organization whose name is left out of the URL, so its repositories are served at `/<repo>` instead of `/<owner>/<repo>`. Repositories of other owners keep the owner in their URL.

base_url.description: GitHub only. The address of your GitHub Enterprise Server, for example `https://github.example.com`. Leave it empty for GitHub.com.

webhook_secret.description: GitHub only. The secret of the GitHub App's webhook. Without it, speicher.md rejects webhook deliveries and picks up changes only on its regular schedule.

app_id.description: GitHub only. The id of the GitHub App, shown at the top of the App's settings page.

private_key.description: GitHub only. The private key of the GitHub App, the content of the `.pem` file GitHub generates.

poll_interval.description: Git only. How often speicher.md checks each repository of this source for new commits, for example `15m`. Repositories can override it.

known_hosts.description: Git only. The SSH host keys of the servers the `ssh://` repositories are fetched from, as `known_hosts` lines. Required as soon as one repository uses an `ssh://` URL; speicher.md connects only to servers listed here.

repos.description: Git only. The repositories this source serves. They are listed here because a plain git server cannot be asked for them.

id.description: Identifies the repository within this source. Choose it once and keep it: speicher.md uses it to recognize the repository when its URL or slug changes.

url.description: The remote URL: `https://host/owner/repo.git` with a `token`, or `ssh://user@host/owner/repo.git` with a `deploy_key`. `http://` and `git://` URLs are refused.

slug.description: The repository's name in URLs. Defaults to `id`. If you change it, the old URLs redirect to the new ones.

branch.description: The branch to publish. Defaults to the repository's default branch.

deploy_key.description: SSH only. The private key of a read-only deploy key, without a passphrase. Required for `ssh://` URLs.

token.description: HTTPS only. An access token that can read the repository. Required for every `https://` URL, also for public repositories.

username.description: HTTPS only. The username that goes with the token. It differs between hosts, for example `oauth2` on GitLab.

poll_interval.description: Overrides the forge-level interval for this repository.

include.description: The include list determines which files will be downloaded from every git repository. Markdown files will be displayed as pages in the reader, while other files such as images can be linked from pages. It defaults to `.md`, `.mdx`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.webp`, `.avif` and `.svg` files. A repository that sets its own `sync.include` replaces this list.

exclude.description: The exclude list determines which files will not be downloaded from any git repository, even when the include list selects them. It defaults to `**/README.md`. A repository that sets its own `sync.exclude` adds to this list.

indexable.description: Set to `false` to keep every repository's pages out of AI assistant search, the sitemap and search engines, unless a repository's pages are already excluded. Repositories cannot turn it back on.

provider.description: Short id of the identity provider the person signs in with. Can be left out when the instance has one provider or sets `auth.default_provider`.

subject.description: Value of the provider's subject_claim. For a magic-link provider the subject IS the lowercased email address.

email.description: The person's email address, matched at every request against the address the identity provider reports at sign-in. Use `subject` for a grant that should survive a change of address.

note.description: Who this entry is for, such as a name and role. Required with `subject`.

until.description: Optional for admins; mandatory for content grants.

githubProvider.description: GitHub as an identity provider for readers. Groups map to org teams as "org/team-slug".

display_name.description: What a reader is offered this provider *as* — "Sign in with Acme Account".

session_ttl.description: Team memberships are read once, at sign-in, so a team somebody has been taken out of keeps working for them until this expires and they sign in again.

connection_idle_ttl.description: If you have a directory configured, this is how long a connection persists while not used. Without a directory, a connection ends with `session_ttl`.

domains.description: Offer this provider only for addresses at these domains. Absent means it is offered for every address.

app.description: The GitHub App of this provider.

client_id.description: The client id of the App. The entry is ignored once client_id names another App.

slug.description: The name of the App in its URLs.

owner_account.description: The GitHub account the App belongs to.

public.description: Whether anyone with a GitHub account can sign in with the App. A private App takes only the members of the account it belongs to. Absent when the App was not created by speicher.md.

directory.description: Optional per-provider directory access. Enables email -> subject resolution at ingest, group-size counts in the pull-request check, and detection of departed principals. Omit it and email grants match on `email_claim` instead, with counts absent from the check.

type.description: graph = Microsoft Graph; github = GitHub organisation API

tenant_id.description: graph: the id of the Entra tenant to read.

client_id.description: graph. Usually a separate app registration from the delegated-flow client: application permissions such as User.Read.All need admin consent.

client_secret.description: graph: the client secret of the directory application.

app_id.description: github. The App id for the directory GitHub App

private_key.description: github. The PEM of the App named

webhook_secret.description: github. This secret is used to sign the webhook deliveries of the App.

cache_ttl.description: How long directory answers are cached before speicher.md asks again.
